title: Dried Chile Paste
summary: Toasted, soaked, and blended guajillo and ancho chiles. Replaces most of the chili powder in taco soup.

steps.title: Clean
steps.text: Snip off the stems, slit the chiles open, and shake out the seeds and pale veins.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: In a dry skillet over medium, press each chile flat for 15 to 30 seconds per side, until it smells toasty and turns a shade brighter. Any black spots or acrid smell: toss it and redo.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover with just-boiled water, weigh down with a small plate, and soak until completely floppy.

steps.title: Taste the water
steps.text: Sip the soaking liquid. If it's bitter, discard it and blend with stock instead.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the chiles with the garlic, onion, salt, and about a cup of liquid until smooth, about ketchup thickness. Chipotles can go in here too.

notes: Brittle chiles are old; good ones bend. Find them in bags in the Mexican aisle.
